title: Describe segregation
intro: Segregation is separation within the mixture that produces an uneven distribution of aggregate sizes or other mixture characteristics. A visibly coarse patch can be a clue, but a crew needs agreed inspection criteria and a traceable location before deciding its cause or treatment.

sections.title: Define Section 502
sections.text:
Section 502.15 of the 2006 specification calls for a homogeneous mixture and uniform surface texture. Its visual classification distinguishes slight, moderate and severe segregation using the amount of stone and remaining binder/fine-aggregate matrix. The project’s agreed comparison areas or photographs support consistent judgement. Temperature differences can also affect paving behaviour; thermal segregation and aggregate-size segregation are related quality concerns but are not interchangeable descriptions.

Track where a pattern occurs: at truck changes, the end of loads, edges, behind a particular part of the screed or at repeated stops. Material handling, stockpiles, truck loading/unloading, hopper management and the feed system all deserve investigation. Do not claim a single cause from a photograph alone. Record station, lane, lift, time, load and observed texture, then notify the responsible lead while the crew can still investigate the process.

The historical top-lift tables 502-I-1 and I-2 address remediation and payment. They include different remedies by severity and counts per lane kilometre. These dated repair descriptions are an exercise in reading a contract, not a field instruction to apply slurry or overlay without approval. Current project specifications and the authorized repair design govern actual work. A payment deduction does not automatically remove the requirement for remediation.

Prevention is a coordinated task. Maintain the specified material-handling and paving process, communicate supply changes early, and avoid scattering coarse material onto a finished surface. When a defect is suspected, preserve evidence and obtain direction before an improvised repair hides the cause.

worked.title: Describe before diagnosing
worked.case: A coarse-looking strip appears near the right edge after three truck changes. The surrounding surface has more fine matrix.
worked.solution: Record the repeated location and timing, photograph from a safe position with a scale and location label, and notify the paving/quality lead. Compare with agreed criteria and inspect the process under authorized conditions. Do not declare severe segregation or choose a repair from appearance alone.

activities.prompt: Write three useful observations and one unsupported conclusion for the case.
activities.answer: Useful: right-edge location; repeated after three truck changes; reduced visible fine matrix relative to surroundings. Unsupported: “the driver caused it” without investigation.
activities.title: Write three useful observations and one unsupported conclusion for the case.

activities.prompt: In the dated Table 502-I-2, a 1 lane-km top lift has 4 slight areas, zero moderate and zero severe. What is the isolated adjustment?
activities.answer: The row requiring 4–5 slight, 0 moderate and 0 severe gives +$500 per lane-km. All three columns and the clause conditions must apply. This does not remove remediation obligations.

activities.prompt: Propose a safe digital defect log and a respectful crew discussion.
activities.answer: Use location, time, lift, load, image, observed texture and status; avoid personal blame. Ask which process changes occurred and agree who will investigate and report the authorized correction.
